data.one_liner: An animated icon package supporting customization like color, animation, hover, and callbacks.
data.what_it_does: Provides an AnimateIcon widget that renders customizable animated icons using Lottie animations behind the scenes. It supports interactive triggers like onTap and onHover, along with adjustable height, width, and color parameters.
use_when: You want to display animated icons using predefined Lottie-based assets.
You need tap and hover callbacks attached to animated icons.
You require basic styling customizations like color and sizing on animated icons.
avoid_when: You need complex physics-based motion or completely custom vector animations.
You are already using an extensive animation suite like flutter_animate or rive and want to avoid extra dependencies.
strengths: Includes built-in support for tap and hover callbacks.
Simple API with customizable color, height, and width parameters.
Cross-platform support for Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
weaknesses: Depends on the lottie package, which might increase app bundle size.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer handling complex animations directly via Lottie files without the restricted wrapper of animated_icon.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a powerful, flexible animation library for animating any Flutter widget rather than being restricted to specific animated icons.

alternatives.name: rive
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer interactive vector animations and state machines over Lottie-based icons.

data.minimal_example:
AnimateIcon(
        key: UniqueKey(),
        onTap: () {},
        iconType: IconType.continueAnimation,
        height: 70,
        width: 70,
        color: Colors.blue,
        animateIcon: AnimateIcons.bell,
      )
